analysis:
The PR adds a CLI-only waitlist client, gate, view and command, plus a test. It does not touch provider WebSocket, attestation, App Attest or inference paths. It adds one new use of the provider login token (A-008): FeatureWaitlist.swift:119-131 sends it as a Bearer header to GET/POST /v1/waitlists on the configured coordinator.

Controls observed:
- Coordinator base is https, or http only to a loopback host (FeatureWaitlist.swift:92-99).
- Redirects are refused by NoRedirects (lines 210, 223-228).
- Cookies are disabled, there is a 10s whole-call deadline, and the response is capped at 64 KiB.
- All coordinator-supplied text (title, summary, start_command, refusal message, feature) goes through printable(), which strips Cc/Cf/newline characters (FeatureWaitlistView.swift:126-133), and --json output is escaped (lines 139-152). That blocks terminal-escape injection from a hostile or compromised coordinator.
- join sends the fixed body {} and nothing about the Mac. The gate (FeatureWaitlistGate.swift) uses constant feature ids. In WaitlistCommand.join the feature used in the URL comes from the coordinator's own catalog, so it is a trusted-coordinator input.

Observations, none qualifying as findings:
- The gate fails open on 404 (FeatureWaitlistGate.swift:54-55). This is a documented UX gate for older coordinators, and the coordinator remains the authority, so it is not a client-side enforcement regression.
- The loopback allowlist includes "[::1]", but URLComponents.host may return "::1" without brackets. That would only fail closed for IPv6 loopback.

Open question for the next pass: A-008 says login records the token issuer in owner-only metadata bound to the token hash. AuthTokenStore.load() is called at WaitlistCommand.swift:36 and the token is sent to whatever coordinator URL the config or --config points to. This diff does not show whether that issuer binding is checked here. I could not verify it, so I am not raising a finding. Operator-controlled config on the user's own Mac is also within the user's authority.
